title: Country-Fried Steak
subtitle: Tenderised beef steak in seasoned breadcrumb crust with white cream gravy
excerpt: Country-fried steak is a Southern American dish: a thin beef steak tenderised by pounding, coated in seasoned flour, fried until crispy, and served with a white cream gravy made from the pan drippings. It is the Southern answer to schnitzel, deeply satisfying and completely unpretentious.
sourceNotes: Country-fried steak (or chicken-fried steak in Texas) is a staple of Southern American cooking. The technique of coating a cheap, tenderised beef cut in flour and frying it was adapted from German and Austrian schnitzel-making techniques brought by immigrants to Texas and the South in the 19th century.

content.text: Country-fried steak uses cheap, tough beef: chuck steak, beef skirt, or blade. The tenderising is essential: pound each steak with a meat mallet or rolling pin until it is about 8 mm thick and has significantly increased in surface area. This breaks the tough muscle fibres and allows the coating to adhere. The gravy is made directly in the pan using the drippings left from frying.
Place each steak between two sheets of baking parchment or cling film. Pound with a rolling pin or meat mallet to about 8 mm thick.
Mix the buttermilk and beaten eggs together in a shallow bowl. In another bowl, mix the flour, cayenne, garlic powder, 1 teaspoon of salt, and 1 teaspoon of black pepper.
Dip each steak in the flour mixture, then the egg mixture, then the flour again. Press the coating on firmly.
Heat the oil in a cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the steaks in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and crispy. Do not crowd the pan. Drain on kitchen paper.

Pour off most of the oil, leaving about 2 tablespoons in the pan along with the drippings. Over medium heat, add 2 tablespoons of flour from the coating bowl and stir for 1 minute. Gradually add the milk, stirring constantly. Simmer until thickened. Season generously with black pepper and salt. Add a dash of hot sauce if using.

items.cause: Coating not pressed on firmly enough, or oil not hot enough so the crust did not set quickly
items.fix: Press the coating on firmly at each stage. The oil should be hot enough that the coating immediately starts to sizzle when the steak goes in.

content.text: Serve with the cream gravy poured over the top and mashed potato or home fries alongside. In the South, biscuits are the classic accompaniment.
